title: 2D Matrix Difference & Reverse Column Indexing
statement: Write a program that declares three 2D arrays of size N x M (named constants initialized to 3 and 4 respectively). Initialize the first array with (row + col)^2 for each location. Take user input for the second array. Initialize the third array with all 0s at declaration time (handling any size of N and M). Update the third array with the difference of the first and second array index by index, with rows filled in reverse column order (e.g., Array1[0][0] - Array2[0][0] is stored in Array3[0][3]). Print all three arrays without hardcoding.
hints: Observe strict PF-lab constraints: avoid banned STL algorithms and classes.

title: validateMatrix: Peak Element & Const Prototypes
statement:
1. Write a C++ function named validateMatrix taking two 2D integer arrays (matrix A and matrix B) and their dimensions (rows and columns). Check consecutive elements in matrix A: if a middle element is greater than both its left and right neighbors (within bounds), mark the corresponding element in matrix B with -1. Write the function definition and call statement.
2. Modify the prototype so matrix A cannot be modified inside the function.
3. Make both 2D arrays parameters with default values in the prototype.
4. Mention prototypes to overload validateMatrix for bool, float, and char datatypes.
5. Write updated prototypes if asked to pass both 2D arrays as pass-by-reference parameters.
hints: Observe strict PF-lab constraints: avoid banned STL algorithms and classes.
